open_points.subject: A19 timestamp representation
open_points.text: Every timestamp the kernel records comes from one clock module; no other part of the kernel reads the wall clock.
open_points.question: In what exact type, timezone, precision and serialization are kernel timestamps returned by `clock_module.now` and stored?
options: timezone-aware UTC datetime with fixed microsecond precision
integer Unix milliseconds
RFC 3339 UTC string
open_points.default_guess: Use a timezone-aware UTC datetime, persisted and serialized as an RFC 3339 string with fixed microsecond precision.

witness.initial: The clock represents an instant containing sub-millisecond precision.
events: An owner inspects the run after storage and reload.
outcomes: The stored and returned timestamp preserves microseconds as an RFC 3339 UTC value.
The timestamp is rounded to integer Unix milliseconds.

open_points.subject: A19 clock readings per operation
open_points.text: Every timestamp the kernel records comes from one clock module; no other part of the kernel reads the wall clock.
open_points.question: For each operation or store change that writes several fresh timestamps, is `now` read once and reused or read separately for every field or event?
options: one reading per surface operation
one reading per store call
one reading per timestamp field
open_points.default_guess: Read once per atomic store call and reuse that instant for every timestamp written by that call.

witness.initial: An injected clock returns a different instant on every call.
events: The request records the approval decision, EffectAttempt and concluding NodeExecution in its successive changes.
outcomes: All timestamps produced by the operation share one instant.
Each timestamp reflects a separate clock reading and differs from the others.
witness.observer: The owner reading the approval, attempt and trace

open_points.subject: A03-3 and A03-4 outcome precedence
open_points.text:
A03-3: trap_raised -> outcome = sandbox_violation   (even if output conforms)

A03-4: outcome = first_of(timeout, resource_exhausted, sandbox_violation, crashed,
                          contract_violation, succeeded)
open_points.question: When a trap is recorded and a higher-priority timeout or resource limit also holds, is the outcome unconditionally `sandbox_violation` or the earlier outcome in A03-4?
options: A03-4 precedence wins
A03-3 is unconditional
open_points.default_guess: Apply A03-4: timeout and resource exhaustion win over a recorded trap.

witness.initial: A function execution has a short wall deadline.
events: Agent code calls `time.time()` and catches the trap.
The same code then busy-loops past the deadline.
outcomes: The execution is `timeout` under A03-4 and Required test 8.
The execution is `sandbox_violation` under the unconditional A03-3 implication.
witness.observer: The agent or owner reading the TrialExecution or NodeExecution

open_points.subject: A03 resource-limit classification
open_points.text: a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`;
open_points.question: What observable event proves that each limit was hit, particularly when `setrlimit` causes an exception or abnormal exit that user code can catch, rather than a parent-visible limit notification?
options: any limit-related exception or signal counts even when caught
only a parent-observed signal or measured excess counts
the runner reports limit hits over its protected channel
open_points.default_guess: Have the runner report recognizable limit exceptions over a protected channel and combine that with parent-observed signals and byte counters.

witness.initial: A function is close to its address-space limit and otherwise returns a conforming value.
events: The function allocates until Python raises `MemoryError`.
The function catches `MemoryError` and returns its conforming output.
outcomes: The allocation counts as a memory limit hit and the execution is `resource_exhausted`.
Because the parent observes a normal return and no defined hit signal, the execution succeeds.
witness.observer: The caller reading the execution outcome

open_points.subject: A13 waiting-element execution
open_points.text: A waiting element can still execute, so M19's "no node can run any more" holds only when nothing waits
open_points.question: Can an element recorded as waiting execute before the human action or resume condition that ends its wait?
options: the waiting element cannot execute; only other ready elements can
the waiting element remains eligible to execute
open_points.default_guess: Treat this as referring to other elements: the waiting element itself cannot execute until its wait is resolved.

witness.initial: A non-read operation element has an `unknown` EffectAttempt and waits with reason `outcome_unknown`.
events: An unrelated request advances the run without the owner resolving the attempt.
outcomes: The element remains waiting and no request is sent, as A11 requires.
The element is eligible to execute because A13 says a waiting element can still execute.
witness.observer: The service and the owner reading the trace

open_points.subject: M17 ProofResult versus A05-6
open_points.text: Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result.
open_points.question: Is a ProofResult a stable function of the flow-version content alone, or may the same `flow_version_id` change from failed to proven when a referenced binding changes status?
options: the result may change with referenced binding status
the same flow version always has the same result
open_points.default_guess: Allow recomputation to change the result when a named binding moves from `proposed` to `accepted`, as A05-6 requires.

witness.initial: A flow version names a binding whose status is `proposed`.
events: An agent proves the flow and receives a phase-1 failure.
The agent proves the same `flow_version_id` again.
outcomes: The second proof is proven under A05-6.
The second proof returns the same failure under M17's identity evidence.
witness.observer: The agent proving or activating the flow

open_points.subject: M19 run success versus A13-7
open_points.text: The run is `failed` when no node can run any more and some node failed, `succeeded` when every node and output concluded successfully.
open_points.question: Does a run succeed when a guarded branch and its flow output conclude `skipped_by_guard`, or does the requirement that every output conclude successfully make it fail?
options: `skipped_by_guard` counts toward successful run completion
every output must produce a value
open_points.default_guess: Count `skipped_by_guard` as successful completion for the run, following A13-7 and A05 rule 4.

witness.initial: A proven flow has a guarded save branch leading to one flow output.
events: The source succeeds with a guard value that disables the save edge.
The save node and output become `skipped_by_guard`.
outcomes: The run is not `succeeded` because the output did not conclude successfully under M19.
witness.observer: The caller of the run and later trace readers

open_points.subject: A05-1 Required tests
open_points.text: A05-1: proof = first_failure(phases[1..9], fixed_order) OR proven
open_points.question: Which Required test must show the complete phase order and the listed condition precedence, rather than only phase 3 preceding phase 7 and ordering among failing edges?
options: one parameterized test covers every adjacent phase and condition boundary
separate tests cover every phase and each multi-condition check
open_points.default_guess: Add parameterized witnesses for every adjacent phase pair and every ordered condition within a phase.

open_points.subject: A05-2 Required tests
open_points.question: Which Required test distinguishes Unicode code-point ordering from UTF-16 code-unit, locale-aware or normalization-based ordering for non-ASCII and supplementary characters?
options: add identifiers containing supplementary and combining characters
declare the existing ASCII `Z`/`a` case sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Add a witness using supplementary-plane and canonically equivalent but differently encoded identifiers.

open_points.subject: A05-3 Required tests
open_points.text: A05-3: can_both_deliver(e1, e2) <-> NOT (guarded_same_port(e1, e2) AND e1.guard_value != e2.guard_value)
open_points.question: Which Required test shows that different guard values are not exclusive when the guards belong to different source nodes or guard ports?
options: add a different-source or different-guard-port pair that phase 6 refuses
infer this case from the formula without a test
open_points.default_guess: Add a test with different guard ports and different values whose edges are refused as able to deliver together.

open_points.subject: A05-5 Required tests
open_points.question: Which Required test proves the maximum over the complete five-member effect-class order rather than only the `read` and `draft-write` cases?
options: test all effect classes and mixed orderings
keep only the read/draft-write example
open_points.default_guess: Add a table-driven test covering every class and mixtures whose maximum is each non-lowest class.

open_points.subject: A05-6 Required tests
open_points.question: Which Required test must demonstrate the `not persisted` part by asserting that proving and reproving create no ProofResult record?
options: inspect the store before and after proof calls
treat changed binding status alone as proof of non-persistence
open_points.default_guess: Add a store-level assertion that proof calls write no ProofResult or equivalent cached record.

open_points.subject: A03-1 Required tests
open_points.text:
A03-1: function_executed -> inside(fresh_bubblewrap_environment)
       environment = {python_stdlib_runtime, code, inputs, exchange_dir, own_proc}
open_points.question: Which Required test shows the fresh user, PID, IPC and UTS namespaces, visibility of only the execution's own processes, and the exact presence of code and inputs?
options: extend the external inspection test to every namespace and environment member
test only mounts, network and exchange-directory freshness
open_points.default_guess: Extend Required test 10 to inspect all namespaces, process visibility and every declared environment member.

open_points.subject: A03-4 Required tests
open_points.text:
A03-4: outcome = first_of(timeout, resource_exhausted, sandbox_violation, crashed,
                          contract_violation, succeeded)
open_points.question: Which Required tests establish every relevant precedence boundary, including `resource_exhausted` over a trap or crash and `crashed` over a simultaneous contract defect?
options: construct a witness for every adjacent precedence pair
test only the timeout/trap/contract combination
open_points.default_guess: Add targeted witnesses for every simultaneously observable adjacent outcome pair.

open_points.subject: A13-1 Required tests
open_points.text: A13-1: advance(run) -> inside(start | approve | resolve | resume | startup_recovery)
open_points.question: Which Required test explicitly demonstrates advancement inside `start` and `startup_recovery`, in addition to approval, resolution and resume?
options: extend the boundary test to all five contexts
rely on unrelated start and recovery tests that do not name A13-1
open_points.default_guess: Add or retag tests that observe advancement inside start and startup recovery and no advancement outside the five contexts.

open_points.subject: A03 trapped-entry-point policy delivery
open_points.text:
- Release build: the frozen list of trapped standard-library entry points —
  closed: A03 rule 4 lists them, and the release passes them as data (A20).
open_points.rule: | константа или таблица политики: пороги, имена, префиксы, закрытые наборы, таблицы правил | константа поставщика данных (§6.10) | `the imported X constant` | имя символа и его тип |
open_points.question: The passage must name the frozen trap list as a specific imported data-provider constant, with one owning module and symbol, rather than merely saying that the release passes it as data.
